claims.event: Compiled the Great Tradition, in which the framework of the Five Elements was first set out in detail.
Expanded on the Hong Fan and interpreted ice on trees as a sign of harm to high ministers.
Sifted classics and commentaries to compile the Five Elements treatise and explained wood failing to be straight or bent.
Collected records from Guangwu onward to examine Han history.
His reign marks the start of Sima Biao's records of Han.
Argued from the classics about portents, and his warnings proved true.
Argued from the classics about portents, and his warnings proved true.
Classified shelled-creature omens as hairy creatures and naked-creature omens as feathered creatures.
In his reign ice formed on trees, and he personally led a naval expedition against Wu.
Led Licheng troops who killed the prefect and seized the commandery, and was suppressed.
Prefect of Licheng killed by Cai Fang's rebels.
Ice formed on trees during his Taixing reign.
Met a violent death two years after the ice portent of Taixing 3.
Met a violent death two years after the ice portent of Taixing 3.
Met a violent death two years after the ice portent of Taixing 3.
Met a violent death two years after the ice portent of Taixing 3.
Attacked the capital, an event read as foreshadowed by the ice portent.
Ice formed on trees during his Yonghe reign.
Marched north, was routed the next year, and was later removed from office.
Led a northern expedition.
Advanced into the passes.
Ice formed on trees during his Taiyuan reign.
Was posted to the northern frontier.
Took the western frontier command.
Was appointed Director of the Secretariat and then General Who Leads the Army.
Became Inspector of Jing Province.
His defeat left the north still divided.
Stirred rebellion in Liang and Yong.
Stirred rebellion in Liang and Yong.
Zhuge Ke's Huainan campaign took place in his Jianxing reign.
Attacked Huainan with heavy levies; his hall beam broke and he was put to death on his return.
In his Taikang reign the temple of Emperor Xuan subsided; he was long ill and died the following year.
His temple ground subsided and a beam snapped.
Directed construction of the new temple with sixty thousand workers.
Recorded uncanny fires in the rear palaces and temple beams breaking.

claims.statement: Put to death after returning from the Huainan campaign.
Killed by rebel troops of Licheng.

claims.event: The Tai'an and Yuankang events took place in his reign.
As Prince of Chengdu sent Lu Ji against the capital, rebuked Jia Mi, and was finally forced to die after defeat.
Pledged himself to Sima Ying, led troops on the capital, was routed and put to death.
As Prince of Changsha uncovered Sima Yong's plot, executed his allies, and was attacked by Sima Ying.
As Prince of Hejian plotted to kill the Prince of Changsha and set up Sima Ying.
An ally of Sima Yong executed by the Prince of Changsha.
While holding Wuchang his regalia sprouted blossoms; he died in rebellion and was disgraced after death.
Interpreted the blossoms in Wang Dun's bell pavilion as a sign that pomp could not last.
Seized the Jin throne; his banner staff broke and he fell after eighty days.
The Taishi omens and Ruan Tianfu's dominance occurred in his reign.
A pillar in his hall glowed through the night.
Hunted and roamed during mourning, set a fashion of license, and his line did not last.
Was punished for blunt remonstrance.
Was put to death for crossing the emperor's will.
Showed no grief in mourning and ended in exile.
Walked and sat with loose deportment, which Guan Luo called demon restlessness, and was later executed.
Called Deng Yang's deportment demon restlessness, foretelling a violent end.
Sported with the crown prince without deference, ignored rebuke, and came to disaster.
Was described by Sima Ying as heir of the realm when slighted by Jia Mi.
Killed Zhao Lun, stayed on as an arrogant regent, and was destroyed.
Was killed by Sima Jiong.
Liu Yi's heir was invested in his Yixi reign.
Was angered when his staff botched his heir's investiture and dismissed Liu Jingshu.
Was dismissed as Director of Gentlemen by Liu Yi.
A talented man of Chen commandery who was supported by attendants and later executed.
Dominated the court with lavish halls and a tilted carriage that others copied.
Rode alone through markets and monasteries and was destroyed.
Observed mourning without grief and hunted without restraint; unending rain followed.
Memorialized that the storms were the penalty of unending rain.

claims.statement: Put to death after his army was routed.
Compelled to commit suicide after defeat.

claims.event: Ignored the Taiping storm warnings and was soon removed.
Explained excessive rain as the penalty of unending rain.
Argued that snow after thunder violated the season.
His case in the Spring and Autumn Annals is compared to Sun Liang's.
Floods of the Taishi era occurred in his reign.
Floods of the Yongning era occurred in his reign.
Floods in Jing Province occurred in his Xiankang era.
The capital flooded during his Yuanjia era.
The capital flooded repeatedly during his Daming era.
The capital flooded in his Taishi era.
Replaced court dress with white silk kerchiefs in a time of famine.
Judged white kerchiefs military garb and He Yan's dress a strange garment.
Interpreted kerchiefs, Wu dress and Jin carriages as omens.
Wore improper dress before Yang Fu, cast the bronze Wengzhong giants, and did not reign long.
Remonstrated about the emperor's improper dress.
Took the giants at Lintao as a good omen and cast bronze men.
Wore women's clothing and his house was destroyed.
Wore a man's cap, an omen of Jie's fall.
Wrote the Discourse on Correct Friendship to remedy harsh Wu customs.
After his reign Wu garments grew long above and short below.
Was wanton and cruel while the people suffered, and lost the state.
Barbarian goods and new household arrangements spread after the Taishi and Taikang eras of his reign.
Interpreted felt headwear, women's quarters, weapon ornaments, hemp piles and Sima Daozi's stalls as omens, and once had the hemp piles scattered.
Seized the central capital by the Yongjia era.
Seized the central capital by the Yongjia era.
Slandered and destroyed the crown prince and was soon ruined herself.
Was destroyed by Empress Jia.
The Record cites his deed in the dance of banners.
As a prince rooted virtue in the east, took the Mandate, and built a capital south of the Yangtze.
Rebelled first in Jing-Chu, drawing many followers.
Died without proper burial.
As Grand General attacked the capital and altered the feather fan.
At his accession the leopard-tail insignia was forgotten, an omen that he would not complete his reign.
Ran wine stalls in his garden, and was deposed, exiled and died a commoner.
Women wore weapon ornaments in the Yuankang era of his reign.
Had kept stalls like Sima Daozi.
Usurped with funeral-like regalia, dominated the west, and fell after eighty days.
Hair fashions and hen omens appeared in his Yuanjia era.
Was driven by Liu Deyuan to Liu Yigong's residence and enjoyed his jests; his favorite Dai Faxing rivaled the throne.
Drove the emperor's painted carriage and asked for a fare.
As Grand Tutor and Prince of Jiangxia was visited at his residence by the emperor in the painted carriage.
Hoarded private money in the Western Garden, a precedent compared to Liu Deyuan's fare-taking.
Rivaled the ruler in power and set the fashion of round-toed shoes.
Commanded at Zheqi, devised a cap style, and later fell to suspicion.
Liu Xiuren's cap and the four-spur chicken appeared in his reign.
A hen turned cock in the Ministry of Justice during his Jingchu era.
Several snail, chicken and fly omens fell in his reign.
Rice in his kitchen turned to snails, and he was executed the next year.
Read snails as signs of war and the hen omen as presaging Jin.
Pacified Liaodong, after which people first spoke of the Cao house yielding to Jin.
Linked the wingless cock to Empress Jia's killing of the heir.
Falsely accused and killed the heir.
Was falsely accused and killed by Empress Jia, as Wang Yin read the wingless cock omen.
A hen in his house crowed; he destroyed Chen Min.
Rebelled and held the lower Yangtze but was destroyed by Zhou Ji.
Held Wuchang and twice attacked the capital.
Chicken omens appeared in his Taiyuan era.
A cock at his house was born without a right wing.
A chicken at his house lacked its right foot.
Chicken omens appeared in his Long'an and Yuanxing eras.
A blue hen at his house turned into a red cock.
Read the Hengyang hen as Huan Xuan's omen.
In his reign hens turned into cocks, a sign later fulfilled by an empress dowager taking part in government.
In his reign the Grand Empress Dowager took part in government, fulfilling the hen omen.
Her orders took effect outside the palace.
A chicken at his house bore four spurs.
The altar tree broke in his Xianning era; his line later perished.
Was born the year after a blue vapor rose from the broken altar tree, fulfilling the Dongguan prophecy.
Held Dongguan as Prince of Wu, later moved to Langya.
Took the blue vapor as the sign of Jin's restoration.
Was executed and his clan wiped out.

claims.statement: Executed the year after the snail omen.

claims.event: Turned back from Xuchang when its south gate collapsed and died in the fifth month.
Zhou Yan's hall leapt from its site in his Taining era.
Joined Wang Dun; his new hall leapt from its site and his clan was destroyed after Qian Feng's revolt.
Was joined by Zhou Yan.
Plotted rebellion, after which Zhou Yan's clan was destroyed.
Was dull and did not cherish worthies; halls collapsed in his reign.
Raised his pennant to march against Huan Xuan and was soon captured by him.
Captured Sima Yuanxian.
Liu Bin's owl-tail omen occurred in his Yuanjia era.
While governing Wu commandery both owl-tails fell from his hall, and he was executed.

claims.statement: Executed soon after the owl-tail omen.
Died in the fifth month after the Xuchang gate collapsed.
